Alphabet's quarterly capital expenditure reached 35.7 billion dollars in the quarter ending March 2026, more than double the 17.2 billion dollars reported exactly one year earlier, the sharpest year-over-year acceleration among the four data points in its series.

The series covers four March quarters spaced a year apart rather than a continuous quarterly run, 6.3 billion in 2023, 12 billion in 2024, 17.2 billion in 2025, and 35.7 billion in 2026. The growth rate itself accelerated in the most recent year. Spending nearly doubled from 2023 to 2024, grew by less than half from 2024 to 2025, then more than doubled again from 2025 to 2026, a pattern of acceleration rather than steady compounding.

Alphabet's 35.7 billion dollars is the second highest among the eight builders here, behind only Amazon's 54.2 billion. Two SEC filings dated within a day of each other in June 2026 disclose a material agreement, changes to corporate governance documents, and a new financial obligation, a concentrated burst of disclosure that lines up with the same quarter in which reported capex jumped most sharply.
